findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId is wrong (checks grantType twice)
findings.body: The constructor checks `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` a second time instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted silently, and the message is also wrong. Should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: Token ID parsing throws on any non-encoded id containing ':' with wrong length
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId splits on the first ':' and throws IllegalArgumentException if the prefix is not exactly 6 chars. Any token id from a non-standard source (or a raw UUID with a colon, or legacy formats) causes an exception rather than falling back to UNKNOWN as done for ids without ':'. Callers (introspection, userinfo) that receive such ids will fail with 500 instead of degrading gracefully.

findings.title: Token type derived from request-wide client attribute, not from the token being created
findings.body: getShouldUseLightweightToken(session) reads session.getContext().getClient(), which is the requesting client, not necessarily the client the token is issued for (e.g. token exchange to another audience, or refresh flows), and the token mapper logic uses the same helper. The encoded token type may not match the actual token format produced, making the encoded context unreliable for the stated use (lightweight detection).

findings.title: Unsynchronized lazy refresh of shared maps on every miss
findings.body: getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut mutate the shared ConcurrentHashMaps during token issuance and token id parsing. The grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts maps are also written without any atomicity across the two maps, so concurrent readers can see them inconsistent. Also, an attacker-supplied unknown shortcut in a token id triggers a full stream scan of provider factories on every request (no negative caching), a cheap DoS amplification.

findings.title: postInit throws on duplicate shortcuts but init/postInit use non-thread-safe HashMap for shortcut tables
findings.body: The shortcut validation compares map sizes, which only detects duplicate shortcuts that collide with the same key; if two grants share a shortcut, one silently overwrites the other in grantsByShortcuts and the sizes still differ only by accident. The size check is an indirect and incomplete duplicate detection. Also OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() has no default, so third-party grant factories break at compile/startup.

findings.title: Cast of getProviderFactory result may throw ClassCastException
findings.body: sessionFactory.getProviderFactory(OAuth2GrantType.class, grantType) returns a ProviderFactory that is cast directly to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without checking; a non-OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation would fail at token issuance.

findings.title: Token ID encoding can throw during token issuance for unregistered grant types
findings.body: initToken calls encoder.encodeTokenId, which throws IllegalStateException when the grant type has no registered shortcut (e.g. a grant set on clientSessionCtx that is not an OAuth2GrantType factory, or tokens created by other paths that never set GRANT_TYPE, where the default 'na' is used). Token creation now fails for flows that previously worked, rather than falling back to a plain id.

findings.title: Blank line removed while adding grant type attribute
findings.body: The edit removes a blank line and inserts setAttribute in its place, which is cosmetic, but the attribute is set after the note and before the client is set; fine. Minor: no functional issue, included only as the diff replaced a blank line.

findings.title: Refresh grant type set after the original grant type was lost; overrides initial value for refreshed tokens
findings.body: validateToken sets GRANT_TYPE to refresh_token on the client session context, but this is only applied on the refresh path. Other paths (e.g. the RefreshTokenGrantType itself, which does not call createTokenResponse) rely on this implicit setting, so the encoded grant in tokens depends on which code path ran, making the encoded grant type inconsistent.

findings.title: Grant type taken from context.getGrantType() which is the raw form parameter
findings.body: context.getGrantType() returns the raw grant_type form parameter, which may be an arbitrary attacker-controlled string. It is stored as the grant type and, if it does not match a registered shortcut, encodeTokenId throws, causing a 500 instead of a proper OAuth error. Validation should happen before use.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher logic is inverted
findings.body: The matcher returns false when the shortcut at substring(3,5) EQUALS the expected shortcut: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. This means a correct token ID is rejected and a wrong one accepted. It also uses substring(3,5) while the encoded format places the grant shortcut at chars 4-5 (index 4..6), so the offset is wrong too.

findings.title: Negative tests use try/catch(RuntimeException) that also swallows the Assert.fail
findings.body: testIncorrectGrantType wraps Assert.fail inside a try catching RuntimeException; AssertionError is not a RuntimeException so it propagates, but the test is still not asserting the specific exception type. Tests for unknown session/token shortcuts and wrong length are missing, and no test covers the 'no ':' ' id parsing or the ClientSessionContext path.

findings.title: Test/code comment mismatch: grantType null-check message
findings.body: The second requireNonNull message reads 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' but checks grantType, misleading maintainers reading the constructor.
